record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Singularities of Mappings
record.original_question: For a stable map-germ (C^n,0) -> (C^p,0) whose restriction to a generic hyperplane in the target has A_e-codimension one, stable germs are classified by their local algebra and that algebra determines which multiple-point space carries the vanishing alternating cycle. What invariant of the local algebra determines that multiple-point-space index?

evidence.quote: the answer to (i) is determined by the local algebra of the germ, since stable germs are classified by their local algebra. What is this invariant of the algebra?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^p,0)$ be a stable holomorphic map-germ, with $p=n+1$ in the standard setting. For each $k\geq 1$, let $D^k(f)\subset(\mathbb{C}^n)^k$ denote the $k$-th multiple-point space (the closure of the set of ordered $k$-tuples of pairwise distinct points sharing the same image with the same target), on which the symmetric group $S_k$ acts by permuting factors; write $H_*^{\mathrm{alt}}(D^k(f);\mathbb{Z})$ for the alternating part of its homology. Assume further that the restriction of $f$ to a generic hyperplane $H\subset(\mathbb{C}^p,0)$ (i.e.\ the map-germ obtained by pulling $f$ back over $H$) has $\mathcal{A}_e$-codimension equal to $1$; equivalently, $f$ admits a one-parameter stable unfolding whose discriminant has a hyperplane section of $\mathcal{A}_e$-codimension one. Under this hypothesis there is a uniquely determined integer $k=k(f)$ such that the vanishing cycle of a stable perturbation is carried by the alternating homology of $D^k(f)$. Because stable map-germs are classified up to $\mathcal{A}$-equivalence by their local algebra $Q(f)=\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}^n,0}/f^*\mathfrak{m}_{\mathbb{C}^p,0}\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}^n,0}$, the integer $k(f)$ depends only on the isomorphism class of $Q(f)$ as a finite-dimensional local $\mathbb{C}$-algebra. 

Problem: Identify an explicit invariant of the finite local $\mathbb{C}$-algebra $Q(f)$ that determines the index $k(f)$ of the multiple-point space carrying the vanishing alternating cycle.
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in a list of open problems on singularities of mappings and concerns the Mond-type vanishing topology for codimension-one map-germs. Web searches turn up related work (e.g. the Journal of Singularities vol. 12 paper and work on vanishing topology of codimension-1 multi-germs) but no source identifying the desired algebraic invariant of the local algebra. The problem appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Singularities of Mappings (Journal of Singularities vol. 12)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems on stable germs, multiple-point spaces and vanishing cycles in the codimension-1 setting.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open problem about which invariant of the local algebra determines the multiple-point-space index.

status_evidence.title: Vanishing Topology of Codimension 1 Multi-germs over R and C
status_evidence.snippet: Studies vanishing cycles in multiple-point spaces for Ae-codimension 1 multi-germs.
status_evidence.claim: Related results exist but do not give a general algebraic invariant determining the index k(f).
